content: Rabbits eat plants such as grass, clover, and leafy greens. Their front teeth never stop growing, so chewing keeps them short. Rabbits can hear well with their long ears and often stay still to stay hidden.
Most owls hunt at night. Their soft feathers help them fly almost silently. An owl cannot move its eyes, so it turns its head to look around.
An octopus has eight arms and can change the color of its skin to blend in. Octopuses are good at solving puzzles and can squeeze through small spaces.

Ocean tides rise and fall about twice a day, mostly because of the pull of the Moon. Tide pools are small pools left on rocky shores when the tide goes out, and they are home to crabs, snails, and sea stars.
The Moon does not make its own light. It reflects light from the Sun. The Moon's shape seems to change during the month because we see different amounts of its sunlit side.
There are eight planets in our solar system. Jupiter is the largest. Mars looks red because of rusty dust on its surface.
Seeds need water, air, and the right temperature to sprout. Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make their own food in their leaves.
A forest is a community of living things. Trees give shelter to birds and squirrels, fallen leaves feed the soil, and insects help flowers make seeds.
A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops. The drops bend the light and split it into colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
A public library lends books for free. Librarians help people find books and information. Many libraries also have story times and reading clubs.
Being brave does not mean never feeling afraid. Courage means doing the right thing, or trying something new, even when you feel nervous.
Good friends listen to each other, take turns, and include others. When friends disagree, they can talk about their feelings and find a fair solution.
Mistakes help our brains learn. Trying again, asking for help, and practicing a little each day make a hard skill easier over time.
Many stories have a beginning that introduces characters and a setting, a middle with a problem, and an ending where the problem is solved and a character has learned something.
